docs.text: Manitoulin Island: The World's Largest Freshwater Island 🌊 Manitoulin Island is the world’s largest freshwater island located in Lake Huron The current name of the island is the English version, via French, of the Ottawa or Ojibwe name Manidoowaaling (ᒪᓂᑝᐙᓕᓐᒃ). It's home to hiking trails, Indigenous communities, and serene beaches. You can even find lakes *on* the island—with islands in them! 🇨🇦

I used to complain about how Lake Huron was no substitute for the ocean. I've finally accepted the fact that even though it's no ocean, it certainly tries to be one and is very good at it. I've been to all five Great Lakes of North America and Lake Huron is and will forever be my favourite Great Lake.

Taiwan’s main island would fit almost entirely inside Lake Michigan, not only in terms of area, but also surprisingly well in shape. Taiwan’s main island covers about 35,808 km², while Lake Michigan has a surface area of roughly 57,757 km². Which other places do you think are similar in size to Taiwan?

So fascinating. "Michigama" got me thinking about "Gitche Gumee" (which is "Lake Superior" in my colonizer language). "gichi-gami" is the Ojibwe name and it means "great sea." "Gitche(e) Gumee" is referenced both in the song "Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald" by Gordon Lightfoot and "Song of Hiawatha" By Henry Wadsworth Longfellow. Thank you for the history lesson. I appreciate it very much.

By my friend’s house. It’s Lake Erie at sunset with a fire hydrant and a concrete post with a car tire around it. I’d call the vibe post-industrial. Lake Erie is the smallest Great Lake and the 11th largest freshwater source in the world.

Beautiful winter afternoon on the southern shoreline of Lake Erie - the shallowest and (by volume) smallest of the Great Lakes, but still the 11th largest lake on the planet. There is a covering of ice near the shoreline but it looks to be very thin right now.
